Package com.nexuslink.protocol.kafka

Record Class ProduceSpec

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.nexuslink.protocol.kafka.ProduceSpec
public record ProduceSpec(String topic, String key, String value, boolean tombstone, List<ProduceSpec.Header> headers, Integer partition, Long timestamp) extends Record
One record to produce, described fully: topic, key, value, headers, an optional target partition and an optional timestamp — and, crucially, the difference between "empty value" and "no value".

That last distinction is not a detail. A record with a null value is a tombstone, and on a compacted topic it is what deletes a key; a producer that can only send strings cannot express it at all, which is why "key + value" is not enough for real Kafka work. Headers matter for the same reason — routing, tracing and schema metadata all live there.

Pure: the record and its validation carry no client, so both are unit-testable.

    • tombstone

      public static ProduceSpec tombstone(String topic, String key)
      A tombstone: a null value against key, which is how a key is deleted from a compacted topic. A tombstone with no key is meaningless — compaction has nothing to match — and validate() rejects it.

    • parseHeaders

      public static List<ProduceSpec.Header> parseHeaders(String text)
      Parses headers written one per line as name: value — the compact form the produce panel edits. Blank lines and # comments are ignored; a line with no colon is skipped rather than becoming a nameless header.
